title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
claim: A new dataset is far larger and richly organized, spanning a hierarchical taxonomy of categories and sub-categories with example samples.
layout: Wide strip: left sample hands, central radial taxonomy chart, right sample hands
description: The crop is a wide, short strip, and the top of the figure is cut off. On the left are two magenta 3D-rendered hands making a thumbs-up, with faded ghost copies showing motion. Cursive magenta caption text above them is partly cropped ("...moving from open palms to a thumbs-up sign"). In the center is the lower part of a multicolor radial sunburst chart. Its inner ring has category segments such as Sport, Gestures and Illustrative/Directive, in green, blue, pink, yellow, cyan and magenta. Its outer ring has many thin sub-category slivers. Curved labels read "Sub-Categories" and "884+ Hours", plus a partly cut number ending in "50". On the right are teal 3D hands with translucent motion trails. Color links each hand sample to its taxonomy category. The eye goes first to the colorful sunburst.
caption: RoMo Hands scales pure-hand text-to-motion data by an order of magnitude. ∼542K in-the-wild bimanual sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps), each paired with five caption granularities (L0–L4) and a three-level action taxonomy. The dataset enables a benchmark of state-ofthe-art diffusion, masked-token, and autoregressive generators adapted to a shared 393-D bimanual hand representation. Interactive dataset statistics, side-by-side benchmark comparisons, dataset explorer, and a 3D motion-grid visualizer are best browsed in the supplementary materials.
abstract: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization. We introduce RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild, text-paired dataset of ~542K sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps) which is an order of magnitude larger than prior work. To ensure high-quality supervision, a stringent dexterity filter discards low-articulation sequences, focusing the distribution on complex bimanual movement. Each clip is paired with five captions at increasing granularities from global semantic tags to atomic finger states, organized under a hierarchical taxonomy. To bridge the gap between body and hand architectures, we propose a novel 393-D bimanual representation that adapts redundant body-motion paradigms to the high-DoF kinematics of hands. Systematic benchmarking of diffusion, masked-token, and autoregressive generators reveals distinct trade-offs under these hand-specific adaptations, including a sharp divergence between semantic alignment and kinematic plausibility. Our dataset, representation, and benchmark establish a rigorous foundation for the next generation of dexterous motion synthesis. Project page: https://romodataset.github.io/romo-hands/.
